title: AI is a helper, not a boss
summary: Why AI is powerful but can be confidently wrong, and the five rules that keep you in control.

slides.sub: AI is a helper, not a boss
slides.say: Welcome to Use AI the Right Way, a free course from Jerry Development. In this first lesson you will learn how to stay in control when you work with artificial intelligence.

slides.h:
AI is fast.
But it can be confidently wrong.
slides.say: AI tools can write, summarize and explain in seconds. But they can also give an answer that sounds perfect and is completely wrong. That is why we need simple rules.

pts: AI is an assistant, not an authority
You are responsible for the final result
Read before you use or send anything
slides.say: Rule one. You are the boss. Treat AI like a smart assistant, not like a final authority. If you send it, publish it or sign it, you are responsible, so always read it first.

pts: Say who you are and what you need
Say the limits: length, tone, level
slides.say: Rule two. Be clear. Tell the AI who you are, what you need, the format you want, and the limits, such as length, tone and level. Clear instructions give much better answers.

pts: If it has no source, do not trust it
slides.say: Rule three. Check the facts. Verify numbers, dates and names with an official source that you open yourself. If an answer has no source, do not trust it blindly.

pts: Never paste passwords or private keys
Never paste other people's private data
slides.say: Rule four. Protect your secrets. Never paste passwords, private keys, wallet recovery phrases or other people's private data into any AI tool. No real helper will ever ask you for them.

pts: Say when content was made with AI
Do not copy other people's work
Do not use AI to cheat or mislead
slides.say: Rule five. Be honest. Say when content was made with AI. Do not copy other people's work, and never use AI to cheat or to mislead people.

slides.h:
Use AI to learn faster,
not to skip thinking.
slides.say: Use AI to learn faster and work better, not to skip thinking. In the next lesson you will learn how to write great prompts. Follow Jerry Development for the full free course.
